title: Chicken Fajitas
subtitle: Spiced chicken with peppers and onions
excerpt: Thin strips of chicken breast tossed in cumin, smoked paprika and chilli flakes, then cooked at high heat with sliced peppers and onions until charred at the edges. The filling is naturally gluten-free; serve it in corn or flour tortillas with whatever toppings you have, from soured cream to pickled chillies.
sourceNotes: Fajitas originated with Mexican ranch workers in Texas in the 1930s who were paid in offcuts of beef; the chicken version became popular in Tex-Mex restaurants during the 1980s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken in the spices and olive oil for up to 4 hours in the fridge before cooking for a deeper flavour.

content.text: The key to fajitas is high heat and not overcrowding the pan. If you pile everything in at once, the chicken and peppers steam rather than char. Work in two batches if needed, or use the largest frying pan you have. The filling is marked as gluten-free; the tortillas you serve alongside are your choice. Corn tortillas keep this fully gluten-free; flour tortillas contain gluten.
Toss the chicken strips with the cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, chilli flakes, half the olive oil and a generous pinch of salt. Mix well to coat.

Heat a large frying pan or wok over a very high heat until smoking hot. Add the remaining oil, then the chicken in a single layer. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes without stirring until the undersides are charred. Toss and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, add the onion and peppers. Cook over a high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing occasionally, until softened and charred at the edges.

Return the chicken to the pan and toss with the peppers and onion for 1 minute to combine. Squeeze over the lime juice and scatter with fresh coriander. Serve immediately with warm tortillas and your choice of toppings.

items.symptom: Chicken is steaming rather than charring
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or too much chicken was added at once
items.fix: Remove the chicken, increase the heat, wait until the pan is smoking, and cook in two smaller batches.

items.cause: Not cooked on high enough heat or stirred too frequently
items.fix: Leave the peppers undisturbed for 2 minutes at a time to get proper colour before tossing.
